The retrieved evidence presents two mutually exclusive positions on whether ancient Egyptians used slaves for pyramid construction. Multiple high-credibility archaeological and Egyptological sources report that the pyramids were built by paid laborers or workers fulfilling a corvée obligation, not by slaves [d1,d3,d5,d6]. These sources cite worker cemeteries, food remains, and graffiti identifying named work teams as evidence of skilled, fed laborers. In contrast, one low-credibility educational site asserts that thousands of slaves were used [d4], and a faith-based source cites biblical and classical accounts alleging Israelite slave labor [d8].

Given the balance of archaeological consensus versus minority or faith-based claims, the dominant view in the retrieved evidence is that slaves did not build the pyramids. However, the presence of contradictory claims within the same scope and time window confirms the conflict type.
